q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is August 24, 2026. Q2 FY2027 for NVIDIA typically ends in July 2026, with earnings release typically occurring in late August/early September 2026. The earnings release has likely already occurred or is imminent (within days). Time to resolution: **essentially immediate** (0-7 days).

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

According to the CURRENT RESEARCH provided, NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue was issued on May 20, 2026 as **$91.0 billion ±2%**, which translates to a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**.

The research also indicates that Wall Street analysts' average estimate is around $91.9 billion, which falls within NVIDIA's guided range.

Since the question asks what **will be** in the earnings release (future tense from the perspective of August 24, 2026), and the guidance has already been publicly issued on May 20, 2026, the most likely outcome is that the actual reported Q2 FY2027 revenue will fall within or very close to the guidance range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

Companies typically beat or meet their own guidance approximately 60-70% of the time, with beats being more common than misses. Given that NVIDIA has built-in conservatism (the ±2% range), the median outcome should be near the midpoint of their guidance: **~$91.0 billion**.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macroeconomic weakness**: A significant slowdown in data center capex spending by hyperscalers or enterprise customers in Q2 FY2027
- **Supply chain constraints**: Manufacturing or logistics issues preventing full revenue realization
- **China restrictions**: Further geopolitical restrictions on GPU exports to China (though guidance already excludes China data center compute revenue)
- **Demand weakness**: Unexpected pullback in AI spending or customer deployments
- **Product execution issues**: Delays or quality issues with new GPU product lines
- The lower bound of $89.2 billion would represent NVIDIA missing at the low end of their own guidance

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected demand**: Hyperscalers accelerating infrastructure buildouts for AI training and inference
- **Pricing strength**: Higher ASPs due to favorable product mix (premium GPU SKUs)
- **Better-than-expected customer deployments**: Earlier-than-anticipated adoption of new products
- **Market share gains**: Competitive losses by AMD or other competitors driving NVIDIA share growth
- The range extends to $115.5 billion, which would represent a ~27% beat above the midpoint of guidance—possible but would require significant upside surprises

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The CURRENT RESEARCH provides the actual issued guidance: **$91.0 billion ±2%** ($89.2B to $92.8B range).

Historical pattern from research: NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 guidance "well above" the prior consensus estimate of $86.84 billion, and the company has demonstrated strong execution in recent quarters with year-over-year growth from $46.7 billion in the year-ago quarter.

Companies typically issue guidance they are confident in meeting, with approximately 65-75% beats to guidance in the semiconductor industry during strong demand periods.

---

## Probability Distribution

The guidance was explicitly stated at $91.0B ±2%, issued on May 20, 2026. As of August 24, 2026, this guidance is fresh (only ~3 months old) and presumably still reflects NVIDIA's expectations.

The most likely outcome clusters around **$90.5 billion to $91.5 billion** (the core guidance level), with a reasonable tail extending to the ±2% boundaries and modest probability of beating guidance above $92.8 billion.

Median (50th percentile): 91000000000

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%** [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This implies a range between $89.2 billion and $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance, which does not assume any data center compute revenue from China, was "well above" the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion from LSEG at the time [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is currently around $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This figure represents a significant increase from the $46.7 billion reported in the year-ago quarter [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
